page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in a narrow column on the right. The signature and catchword sit at the foot.

main_text.p: Secunda dicitur Cornea, quæ durior est, è dura meninge orta, & omni ex parte toti oculo obnata.II.
Tertia dicitur Uvea, quæ est à tenui meninge orta, instar iridis versicolor.III.
Quarta est Retiformis tunica, exi-stens ex nervo optico ad posteriorem o-culi partem dilatato.IV.
Nervus opticus est primum nervorum par, à cerebri basi ortum, quod utrum-que oculum petens, in latam oculi tunicam expansum, oculo animales defert spiritus.Nervus opticus,
Quinta dicitur Aranea, quæ tenuis est, à tenui meninge orta, telam aranea-rum referens, in medio oculi humorem cristallinum in sua sede continens, & vitreum ab albugineo discernens.
Hæ fuerunt tunicæ : Humores oculi sunt tres.Oculi hu-mores tres.
Primus dicitur Aqueus, fluidus seu albugineus, qui est humor aquæ modo pel-lucidus, in anteriore parte oculi inter corneam & uveam comprehensus.I.
Secundus dicitur Vitreus (quod vitri liquefacti & fusi sit similis) qui in posteriori oculi parte sedes est cristallini.II.

page.notes: The scan is faint and shows show-through from the facing page (mirrored text and marks in the margins and the middle of the text block), which is left out. The word "fusi" and "sit" in the parenthesis of the Vitreus paragraph are only partly legible and may be misread. The spelling "cristallinum" follows the printed "cristallinum". The margin notes "I.", "II.", "III.", "IV." are printed as separate numbers beside their paragraphs.
